transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~37m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (HorizonX CTO), Lena (ML Eng), Marcus (Platform)

Summary (auto): Quick context on current OpenAI usage, pain points (cost and variability), exploration of Dedicated commit, questions about running vLLM/TGI model stacks, and how Redwood ensures eval parity. Next steps captured at end.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE working with HorizonX — Priya, our solutions engineer, is on as well.
00:08 Samir: Hey Jordan, thanks. Samir here, I run infra at HorizonX, with Lena and Marcus.
00:13 Lena: hi everyone.
00:17 Priya: quick intro from our side, I'm Priya, I work with a few customers on migrations and runtime compatibility.
00:23 Jordan: goal for today — understand your stack, traffic, and success criteria for a move off OpenAI to either Redwood Hosted or Dedicated or Private.
00:32 Marcus: we're mainly looking at Dedicated tbh, cost predictability is the big driver, also data residency.
00:39 Samir: right we saw token costs spike last quarter and latency jitter, that hurt product metrics.
00:45 Jordan: makes sense — can you describe current architecture and what models/APIs you call?
00:52 Lena: sure, we use OpenAI's chat endpoints for two features: a conversation assistant and an internal summarization pipeline. Model mix is about 70% chat completions using gpt-4-ish and 30% embedding calls, some small rerankers. We batch embeddings.
01:10 Priya: are you running any self-hosted inference today like vLLM or TGI?
01:14 Lena: not in production; we have a dev experiment with vLLM on a single NVLink box but it's not stable and doesn't match OpenAI quality on a few prompts.
01:24 Jordan: what does parity mean for you — token-level, semantic similarity, or business metric?
01:30 Samir: business metric — accuracy of extracted entities for our support triage and latency under 200ms p50 on short queries.
01:38 Marcus: and compliance — we need some logs retained for audit for six months and SSO/SAML integrated.
01:45 Priya: Redwood Dedicated supports VPC deployments and KMS/HSM integrations, and our Console gives audit logs and per-route tracing. For latency, we can pin model variants and route shorter queries to lower-latency configurations.
01:59 Samir: about compatibility — you mentioned vLLM and TGI in your docs. If we containerize our current TGI stack, can it run on Redwood Dedicated?
02:09 Priya: short answer: yes, but there are nuances. Redwood Dedicated's runtime supports standard HF formats and most conversion paths. vLLM and TGI are generally compatible, but performance and KV-cache behavior vary. We'll want to run a compatibility benchmark with your exact model and prompt set.
02:25 Lena: the worry is eval parity — our dev runs on vLLM produce slightly different outputs vs OpenAI and that breaks downstream heuristics. How do you surface regressions?
02:35 Priya: we recommend running a two-phase eval: first, dataset-level automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/emb-similarity + our custom scoring tied to your heuristics), then side-by-side human eval for samples where automated metrics diverge. We also support regressions alerts integrated into the Console tied to prompt sets.
02:52 Jordan: also we can offer a staged rollout — start Hosted (to validate functional parity under low volume) then Dedicated for throughput and predictable cost, with a canary route back to Hosted or fallback models if regressions appear.
03:06 Marcus: pricing and sizing — what does Dedicated look like for our traffic? Current QPS is about 8 req/s across short chat and batch embeddings peak around 80 req/s for embeddings jobs.
03:18 Priya: ok rough ballpark: if you need low-latency chat at p50<200ms, we'd look at a mix of GPU types — A10G/P4 for embeddings batching and A100/RTX-class for high context chat. We'll produce a sizing doc but need your prompt length distribution and concurrency.
03:33 Samir: we'll send the traffic profile.
03:36 Lena: also, our internal cost target is 40% less than current OpenAI spend for the same throughput.
03:43 Jordan: understood — our Optimize tooling and quantization/ batching suggestions often get customers into that range, depends on models and eval tolerances.
03:50 Samir: questions on security — we need SOC2 + ISO mentioned and SSO. Do you provide legal addenda?
03:56 Jordan: we have SOC 2 Type II, ISO certs and standard data processing addenda; AE will include security pack and legal contacts.
04:04 Priya: for Private deployments, if you go air-gapped, we can do an on-prem package; otherwise VPC with customer-managed subnets and KMS integrated is common.
04:14 Marcus: good. On the model side — you host open models in the catalog, do you host proprietary customer models?
04:20 Priya: yes, in Dedicated we can host your model artifacts behind your VPC, and you can pin versions. For models converted from TGI/vLLM, we store the converted artifacts in a customer-controlled bucket if requested.
04:33 Lena: what about latency regressions with vLLM? Our dev's vLLM run was inconsistent due to KV cache misses and batching config.
04:41 Priya: right — runtime tuning matters. Redwood's serving runtime optimizes KV cache handling and continuous batching; we tune kernel selections based on sequence length distribution. In practice we've reduced variance for customers by stabilizing caching and routing. But we need to test with your prompt distribution.
04:58 Jordan: do you have any hard requirements on output determinism? Some customers accept sampling differences if business metrics hold.
05:06 Samir: determinism is not required but we need consistent downstream performance; we can tolerate some variance if entity extraction precision stays within 2% of current.
05:15 Priya: noted — we'll run the scorer against your golden set.
05:19 Marcus: integration — what does deployment look like? API compat with OpenAI?
05:24 Jordan: Redwood Hosted provides an OpenAI-compatible endpoint shim for common routes (chat/completions/embeddings) to make migrations easier; Dedicated can expose the same API surface or direct SDKs depending on preference.
05:38 Lena: that shim — does it handle function calling and streaming?
05:42 Priya: yes we support streaming and function-calling primitives, though for function-calling semantics there's some version mapping to be aware of; we'll document differences.
05:52 Samir: on billing — if we commit to Dedicated, how do overage and burst work?
05:57 Jordan: Dedicated has reserved capacity with configurable burst policies; overage pricing and burst credits are in the sizing proposal we'll send. We can also configure autoscale policies for non-critical routes.
06:09 Lena: any customers who've moved from OpenAI and validated parity?
06:13 Priya: several — we ran a case with Nova (internal name), they moved to Dedicated and used our eval suite to validate parity then staged traffic. One early hiccup was model tokenization differences on a custom tokenizer, which we caught in preflight.
06:29 Samir: tokenization — we use a custom tokenizer for some domain-specific tokens; can you host tokenizers?
06:35 Priya: yes, we support custom tokenizers as part of model artifacts; that is part of the compatibility checklist.
06:42 Jordan: circling back to migration path — recommended approach we propose: 1) Preflight compatibility run on a small dataset (Priya provides checklist), 2) Hosted pilot to test functional parity under real traffic, 3) Dedicated sizing and commit, 4) Canary cutover with monitoring and automatic fallback.
06:58 Marcus: timeline question — we want to be off OpenAI for core internal workloads by end of Q2. Is that realistic?
07:04 Priya: with the checklist and the data you share, a Hosted pilot within 2-3 weeks and Dedicated commit in 4-6 weeks is feasible, assumes no major model conversion blockers.
07:15 Samir: cool. A few technical nitty-gritty: do you allow custom runtime flags for vLLM or fine-grained GPU affinity?
07:23 Priya: we expose runtime config knobs — batch size, kv cache policies, kernel selection hints; for Dedicated we can work with your infra team to tune GPU affinity but full low-level control depends on the deployment model (Private on-prem gives most control).
07:37 Lena: latency SLOs — can you show us historical p50/p95 for similar workloads?
07:43 Jordan: we'll attach latency dashboards from comparable customers in the follow-up; it's part of the sales kit.
07:50 Samir: legal/contracting — who do we speak with for the data processing addendum?
07:54 Jordan: I'll include our legal contact in the follow-up email and include the security pack.
07:59 Marcus: ok. Any blockers from our side?
08:02 Lena: we need to confirm retention limits and whether logs can be filtered to remove PII before retention.
08:09 Priya: we support configurable retention per route and can redact or avoid storing full request bodies if that's required; we also offer audit-only modes.
08:18 Samir: great.
08:20 Jordan: let's recap next steps — Jordan will send sizing/pricing and security pack; Priya will share the benchmark checklist and sample prompts; HorizonX to send traffic profile and tokenization notes. We'll schedule a technical deep dive focused on vLLM/TGI compatibility week of 3/16.
08:38 Lena: that works.
08:40 Samir: thanks everyone.
08:42 Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up.

Notes: transcription includes some auto-caption errors — e.g., 'kv cache' sometimes transcribed as 'kay vee cache', product names may be slightly off. References to Nova are anonymized customer examples.

Action items (captured): Jordan Hayes to send Dedicated pricing + security pack; Priya Mehta to share benchmark checklist and sample prompts; HorizonX (Samir/Lena) to provide traffic profile and tokenizer details.

End of call.
